author: Pebblous Data Communication Team
headline: AutoDNA Explained: Six Agents, Results and Limits
text: A laboratory now exists that takes one request typed in plain words and carries a DNA experiment from design through execution by itself. AutoDNA, which researchers at Shanghai Jiao Tong University published in Nature on November 4, 2026, has six AI agents work the procedure out in conversation, write the code that drives the machines, and send it to more than 20 instruments. The longest demonstration was a round trip that put digital information into DNA and read it back out. It came to 11,382 hardware steps over about 203.5 hours, a little more than eight days, and the original sentence came back intact. Sources: the Nature paper An AI-native experimental laboratory for autonomous biomolecular operations.
